title: Orionid Meteor Shower: Halley's Comet Debris Peaks Tonight + X-energy + All-In + Solana's Alpenglow
summary: Dust from Halley's Comet peaks tomorrow night — the full story of the Orionids, from records in 240 B.C. to the comet's return in 2061, plus today's American company: X-energy, a Web3 Watch upgrade, and the All-In podcast's Dylan Field interview.
body:
Tomorrow night, dust left behind by the most famous comet in history rains through our sky. The Orionid meteor shower is active now and peaks the night of October 21–22.

THE PAST. The story starts with records, not telescopes: astronomers in China logged this comet as early as 240 B.C. In 1705 Edmond Halley saw that three famous comets were one and predicted its return — the prediction held on Christmas Day 1758. In 1986 a spacecraft armada met the comet, and ESA's Giotto photographed its dark core. The dust it sheds crosses Earth's path twice a year.

THE PRESENT. The October crossing is the Orionids, named for Orion. This year the bright Moon is the one catch: best viewing is before dawn, after the Moon sets, at ten to twenty meteors an hour under dark skies. A G1 geomagnetic storm watch also ran October 19–20.

THE FUTURE — confirmed only. A full moon follows on October 26, the sister Eta Aquariid shower arrives next May, and Halley's Comet — which turned for home in December 2023 — returns in 2061.

In the after-story slots: The Web3 Watch — Solana's Alpenglow upgrade, a new consensus engine scheduled to activate October 21 at epoch 1064, targeting finality near 150 milliseconds. And The Big Shows — All-In episode 438 with Figma's Dylan Field, reviewed from the full episode. Not financial advice.

company.name: X-energy
company.text: Founded in Rockville, Maryland, X-energy builds advanced pebble-bed nuclear reactors and the TRISO-X fuel that powers them — billiard-ball-sized fuel pebbles designed to contain their own fission products. On October 19, 2026, X-energy, Amazon and AEP Indiana announced a study of a new plant in Indiana. Company facts only: no prices, no predictions.
